args.prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. A frame from a camera move through the same house: the same room, products, light and grade as the attached crops of the master photographs (reference 1; the neighbouring room as reference 2). They are cut from photographs taken from other cameras and show the look only; the clay alone sets the framing, the position and the size of everything; render only what this clay shows. 24 mm shift lens at 1.2 m, level, straight verticals, all sharp.

2. LIGHT. Soft north daylight from the bedroom window, out of frame to the left, no sun. Exposed for white: the panelled wall clean white; the corridor through the door bright and still detailed, its roof slot glowing. The bedroom wall falls off half a stop to the right; fine shadow lines in the panelling grooves; the planter lit on its left face, darker on its right. Dense contact shadows under the nightstand and the planter. Ceiling a touch darker. Real contrast, never milky. 4600 K: whites white, never cream, pink or grey. Lamps 2700 K, low, shadowless: the wall lamp glows through its fabric and lays a small warm pool on the nightstand top and a soft fan on the panelling.

3. MATERIALS. Matte mineral paint #F4F1EC; bed wall panelled to 1.25 m in painted warm-white tongue-and-groove, slim oak cap. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E. Bed, headboard, nightstands: oiled oak #C8A27A, satin sheen, a long soft window highlight along the nightstand tops.

4. PRODUCTS, one per line, each on its clay placeholder:
b. WALL LAMP, just above the panelling cap, x 0.08-0.13, y 0.37-0.45: one flush beige linen-look wave lamp, half the nightstand's width, hardwired (its pair is out of frame).
e. PLANTER, standing free in front of the panelling, x 0.19-0.36, y 0.21-0.98: natural seagrass belly pot cover, a tall olive tree, crown below 1.75 m.
h. CANDLE HOLDERS, on the nightstand, x 0.08-0.13, y 0.66-0.71: two hand-sized honed travertine pedestals, unlit candles 15 and 10 cm.
i. PILLOWS, x 0.00-0.02, y 0.66-0.72: two natural washed-linen pillowcases.
j. THROUGH THE DOOR: exactly the corridor of reference 2, the gallery of three prints on its left wall, the paper lanterns, the glowing hall and living room at its end; the opening on the right a soft lit pass in the wall colour, nothing in it.

5. NOT IN FRAME: floor lamp, tray, carafe, glass, books, phones, clocks, rug, basket, bedroom ceiling lamp, window, socket, cable, text, people. No sun patches, beams, bloom, haze, halos, HDR, grain or vignette.
